{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the bottom line of the fish from the nose out to the low point of the belly, about 40 dominoes. That is the whole underside of the body and one of the two long outlines that make the fish readable. The finished run connected roughly 121 of 124 standing dominoes, so the picture should fall almost entirely as a fish.

Execution: I took the bottom line as soon as Sofia's sketch went up and traced it straight from the start. I kept steady, steady-paced batches, with no redo needed on my stretch. I reported when I reached the low point so Hana could join onto my last domino and keep it one unbroken run. After that I inspected the crossing area twice and checked a possible stray domino before the tail. When it looked fine, I left it alone rather than risk a bump.

Collaboration: I split the bottom line cleanly with Hana, agreeing on the handoff point and where she would pick up. I answered quickly when she asked where I was, which avoided overlap and idle time. I kept the table informed on where my hands were and what I was checking. Once the build was done, I backed the group decision to keep hands off, and I reminded everyone of it during the final minutes so nobody bumped the run.

Leadership: I kept the mood light and the table energised through the last stretch, with time calls and encouragement. I also modelled the discipline of stopping once the work was done. Overall I believe my bottom-line work and handoff were central to the result. I would put my share at about 30 percent of the table's outcome.", "my_share_percent": 30}
